segments.text: Morning on the counter.
New keys in my hand.
Same four walls standing, but I finally understand.
The room remembers footsteps.
The glass remembers rain.
But a house is not a prison when you name it once again.
I changed the lock, changed the number, changed the road I take.
Kept the parts that made me human, left the parts that made me break.
First day back, black coffee train shaking through the town.
Fear sat beside me whispering.
I turned the volume down.
My friend called from the corner said, "You do not have to hide." I wore the clothes I wanted and I walked there with my stride.
No report can hold my future.
No old room can set my speed.
Every choice becomes a heartbeat.
Every heartbeat proves I lead.
Sometimes his voice comes back at night, but it gets smaller in the light.
I do not owe the dark my name.
I know the difference now between love and blame.
After the door, I found the sky.
After the fear, I learned to try.
No one owns the road beneath my feet.
I turn the silence into a beat.
If you are waiting where the shadows start, leave one light on, follow your heart.
I am not what I survived before.
I am the life after the door.
Back in class pen moving, future written in the margin.
Teacher asked my name.
I said it like a promise, not a bargain.
At work, I took the late shift, signed my hours, paid my rent.
Small things look like mountains when your life was time well spent.
I met my sister at the station, saw the courage in her eyes.
We did not need a rescue speech just room enough to rise.
She said the world is still uncertain.
I said then we learn the street.
Two survivors making maps from every place we used to retreat.
If the old alarm rings loud, I do not disappear into the crowd.
I breathe, I call, I state the truth.
The future is a door and I decide what passes through.
After the door, I found the sky.
After the fear, I learned to try.
No one knows the road beneath my feet.
I turn the silence into a beat.
If you are waiting where the shadows start, leave one light on, follow your heart.
I am not what I survived before.
I am the life after the door.
Brother, you can stand beside me, but you cannot live my life.
You can hold the extra flashlight.
I will choose the road at night.
No crown, no debt, no borrowed throne, no savior in the frame.
The strongest thing you gave me was the space to say my name.
And if another voice is shaken on the other side of fear, we will not demand a perfect story before we draw near.
We will make a place with exits.
We will leave the hallway bright.
We will call survival by its name and walk it in the light.
After the door, I found the sky.
After the fear, I learned to try.
No one knows the road beneath my feet.
I turn the silence into a beat.
I open what I want to open...and I step into the light
